targetTexts.1: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
targetTexts.2: The tongue of the wise commends knowledge, but the mouth of the fool spouts folly.
targetTexts.3: The eyes of the LORD are in every place, observing the evil and the good.
targetTexts.4: A soothing tongue is a tree of life, but a perverse tongue crushes the spirit.
targetTexts.5: A fool rejects his father’s discipline, but whoever heeds correction is prudent.
targetTexts.6: The house of the righteous has great treasure, but the income of the wicked is trouble.
targetTexts.7: The lips of the wise spread knowledge, but not so the hearts of fools.
targetTexts.8: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable to the LORD, but the prayer of the upright is His delight.
targetTexts.9: The LORD detests the way of the wicked, but He loves those who pursue righteousness.
targetTexts.10: Discipline is harsh for him who leaves the path; he who hates correction will die.
targetTexts.11: Sheol and Abaddon lie open before the LORD—how much more the hearts of men!
targetTexts.12: A mocker does not love to be reproved, nor will he consult the wise.
targetTexts.13: A joyful heart makes a cheerful countenance, but sorrow of the heart crushes the spirit.
targetTexts.14: A discerning heart seeks knowledge, but the mouth of a fool feeds on folly.
targetTexts.15: All the days of the oppressed are bad, but a cheerful heart has a continual feast.
targetTexts.16: Better a little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure with turmoil.
targetTexts.17: Better a dish of vegetables where there is love than a fattened ox with hatred.
targetTexts.18: A hot-tempered man stirs up strife, but he who is slow to anger calms dispute.
targetTexts.19: The way of the slacker is like a hedge of thorns, but the path of the upright is a highway.
targetTexts.20: A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish man despises his mother.
targetTexts.21: Folly is joy to one who lacks judgment, but a man of understanding walks a straight path.
targetTexts.22: Plans fail for lack of counsel, but with many advisers they succeed.
targetTexts.23: A man takes joy in a fitting reply—and how good is a timely word!
targetTexts.24: The path of life leads upward for the wise, that he may avoid going down to Sheol.
targetTexts.25: The LORD tears down the house of the proud, but He protects the boundaries of the widow.
targetTexts.26: The LORD detests the thoughts of the wicked, but the words of the pure are pleasant to Him.
targetTexts.27: He who is greedy for unjust gain brings trouble on his household, but he who hates bribes will live.
targetTexts.28: The heart of the righteous ponders how to answer, but the mouth of the wicked blurts out evil.
targetTexts.29: The LORD is far from the wicked, but He hears the prayer of the righteous.
targetTexts.30: The light of the eyes cheers the heart, and good news nourishes the bones.
targetTexts.31: He who listens to life-giving reproof will dwell among the wise.
targetTexts.32: He who ignores discipline despises himself, but whoever heeds correction gains understanding.
targetTexts.33: The fear of the LORD is the instruction of wisdom, and humility comes before honor.
